title: Workato Alternatives for B2B SaaS Teams (September 2026)
summary: The best Workato alternatives for B2B SaaS teams in September 2026, compared on white-label UI, per-tenant pricing, and connector depth.
body_markdown:
Most Workato comparisons are written for IT and operations teams, which is great if that's you. But if you're a CPO or Head of Partnerships at a B2B SaaS company trying to ship customer-facing integrations, the criteria change entirely. Things like white-label UX, per-tenant pricing, and control over data processing logic matter a lot more than connector count (and yes, connector count still matters, just less than everyone pretends). We'll cover seven alternatives with that lens.


**TLDR:**


- Workato's enterprise contracts run well into six figures annually, making it a tough sell for SaaS product teams
- Most tools on this list (Zapier, Tray.ai, MuleSoft) were built for internal automation, not customer-facing integrations
- White-label embedded UI and per-tenant pricing are the two capabilities where nearly every Workato alternative falls short
- hotglue is purpose-built for embedded B2B SaaS use cases, with open-source connectors, Python-based data pipelines, and SOC 2 Type II compliance


## What Is Workato and How Does It Work?


Workato is a low-code integration and automation tool built for enterprise IT and operations teams. It lets non-developers connect internal business systems by building "recipes": step-by-step workflow automations that trigger actions across apps when certain conditions are met. If you've used HubSpot workflows or Zapier, the mental model is familiar: pick a trigger, add steps, define logic, publish.


The recipe builder is visual and approachable for business users, which is a deliberate design choice. Workato targets RevOps, IT, and automation teams who need to wire together tools like Salesforce, Workday, NetSuite, and ServiceNow without writing custom code. It covers over 1,200 app connectors, and its pricing scales based on usage, making it an enterprise-grade option, though one that tends to come with enterprise-grade costs to match.


Where Workato excels is internal automation: syncing data between systems your own team uses, automating approvals, routing records, or triggering notifications. It was built for that use case and does it well.


## Why Consider Workato Alternatives?


Workato is a solid choice if you're a large enterprise with a dedicated IT or RevOps team managing internal automations. Cross-system workflows between Salesforce, Workday, and ServiceNow? It handles that well. But several recurring gaps push B2B SaaS product teams toward other options.


Pricing is the first friction point. Workato's enterprise contracts can run well into six figures annually, and the task-based billing model makes costs harder to predict as usage scales. For mid-market SaaS companies, that structure is hard to defend when integrations are a product feature, not an internal operations budget line.


The UX model is the deeper issue, though. Workato exposes its own workflow builder to end users. One prospect we spoke with described it as "building a Zap or a HubSpot workflow," which is fine for internal power users, but not what customers expect when they open your product. They want integrations that feel native to your app, not a third-party automation tool bolted on.


Workato is also a generalist. It was designed for IT-led internal automation, so its embedded product (Workato Embedded) is an adaptation of that model and not something purpose-built for customer-facing integration. The distinction matters. B2B SaaS teams building integrations for their own customers need white-labeled UX, tenant-scoped data handling, and developer control over transformation logic. Workato's architecture makes that difficult by design. For a deeper breakdown of how[embedded iPaaS](https://hotglue.com/blog/what-is-embedded-ipaas) differs from general automation tools, that distinction is covered in full elsewhere.


The fit question is simple: if your team is connecting internal tools for your own operations, Workato is reasonable. If you're a CPO or Head of Partnerships shipping integrations inside your product for paying customers — the person who gets tagged in Slack at 2am when an integration breaks, and who also has to explain it to the customer the next morning — you'll likely outgrow it fast. Ownership of the integration layer typically sits with the product or partnerships lead, not IT, which is exactly why the tool choice matters so much.


## Best Workato Alternatives in September 2026


### 1. hotglue (Best Overall)


Built from the ground up for B2B SaaS teams shipping customer-facing integrations. Unlike most tools here, hotglue was designed for embedded use cases, not internal IT automation.


- White-label widget embeds natively inside your product, so customers never leave your UI to set up integrations
- Tenant-based pricing means costs stay predictable as your customer base grows, no surprise bills from task volume spikes
- Python-powered data processing with open-source connectors give engineering teams full control over data logic
- SOC 2 Type II compliant; data is processed and delivered, never stored


Best for: Product and engineering teams building native integrations for paying customers.


Bottom line: If you want integrations that feel like part of your product, this is where to start.


### 2. Tray.ai


An enterprise iPaaS with[AI orchestration](https://tray.ai/platform/intelligent-ipaas/) and 700+ connectors. Strong for governed, IT-managed automation across complex business systems.


- AI-assisted workflow building reduces manual configuration time for operations teams
- Supports agents, MCP, and process automation across enterprise systems
- Enterprise governance and audit trails keep compliance teams happy


Good for: IT and RevOps teams. Key limitation: Not purpose-built for embedded customer-facing integrations. Bottom line: Powerful, but built for internal workflows.


### 3. Zapier


The most widely recognized automation tool. Offers a large app library with thousands of connections across a range of paid plans.


- Simple trigger-action model makes it accessible to non-technical users quickly
- Huge app library covers the long tail of SMB software tools
- Easy setup with no coding required for basic workflows


Good for: SMB internal automation. Key limitation: Task-based billing scales unpredictably; no embedded product use case. Bottom line: Great for personal automation, wrong tool for SaaS product teams.


### 4. Pipedream


Developer-first automation using a credit-based billing model. Acquired by Workday in late 2025.


- Code-native workflow building with full flexibility for complex logic
- Supports Node.js and Python steps natively, which developers appreciate
- Large connector library covers most common SaaS APIs


Good for: Developer automation and internal tooling. Key limitation: Acquisition uncertainty; no white-label or embedded UX. Bottom line: Solid for dev workflows, not for shipping customer integrations.


### 5. MuleSoft


Salesforce's enterprise integration offering.[Starts at $2K/month](https://www.salesforce.com/mulesoft/anypoint-platform/pricing/) with API governance and agent management built in.


- Full API lifecycle management for organizations running many internal services
- Deep Salesforce ecosystem integration for revenue and CRM workflows
- Enterprise-grade governance with role-based access controls


Good for: Large enterprises with dedicated integration teams. Key limitation: High cost and steep learning curve. Bottom line: Overkill for most B2B SaaS product teams.


### 6. Paragon


An embedded integration tool targeting SaaS companies, with similar positioning to hotglue and a visual workflow builder for end users.


- White-label integration UI keeps your product branding intact for customers
- Pre-built connectors for common SaaS tools reduce initial setup time
- Workflow editor is accessible to non-developers on your customer's team


Good for: SaaS teams wanting a low-code embedded integration layer. Key limitation: Less control over data transformation logic compared to a code-first approach. Bottom line: A reasonable embedded option, though with less depth on ETL and custom connectors.


### 7. Boomi


Dell's cloud integration offering with a long enterprise track record and a visual low-code builder.[Pricing starts at $99/month](https://boomi.com/pricing/) for a pay-as-you-go entry tier, with enterprise contracts typically running well into five figures annually.


- Wide connector library covers most enterprise and mid-market software stacks
- Strong data mapping tools for organizations moving data between complex systems
- SOC 2 and compliance certifications meet enterprise security requirements


Good for: Mid-to-large enterprises with internal integration needs. Key limitation: Enterprise pricing and IT-centric design make it a poor fit for embedded SaaS use cases. Bottom line: Mature and reliable, but not built for customer-facing product integrations.

## FAQ


### Why do B2B SaaS teams look for Workato alternatives?


Workato was built for internal IT and RevOps automation, not for shipping customer-facing integrations inside a product. B2B SaaS teams run into friction with its task-based billing (costs spike unpredictably), its workflow builder UX (not something your customers should see inside your app), and its limited support for white-labeled, tenant-scoped integration experiences.


### What should you look for in a Workato alternative for customer-facing integrations?


Focus on four things: white-label UI that embeds natively in your product, per-tenant pricing that stays predictable as your customer base grows, developer control over transformation logic, and connectors that cover the systems your customers actually use, including on-premise accounting tools like QuickBooks Desktop and Sage 300 CRE.


### When does switching from Workato to hotglue make sense?


If your team is shipping integrations as a product feature for paying customers, the switch makes sense as soon as you feel friction from Workato's internal-automation architecture. Two clear signals: when your customers are seeing a third-party workflow builder instead of a native integration experience, or when your engineering team loses visibility into connector logic because the codebase is a black box.


### How does hotglue's pricing model compare to Workato's for growing SaaS products?


Workato uses task-based billing, which scales unpredictably as usage grows. Hotglue charges per active tenant on a 30-day rolling window, so your costs scale with your customer count, not with data volume or task frequency. A single tenant connecting to multiple connectors counts as one tenant, not several.


### Can hotglue replace Workato for teams that need both embedded customer integrations and Python-based data transformation?


Yes. Hotglue combines a white-label embedded widget with a Python-powered transformation layer backed by Pandas and Dask, running on JupyterLab with Git integration and separate dev and production environments. That gives engineering teams the same code-level control they'd expect from a custom build, without the ongoing maintenance cost of managing API changes and connector rebuilds in-house.
